title: Close the length-22 seven-label word census: all splits excluded, f(7) = 24 in the prefix-walk model (no new κ)
body:
## Result

**Finite census result (exhaustive enumeration with written pruning proofs) inside PR943's singleton prefix-walk model.** There is no restored universal length-22 seven-label word, so **f(7) = 24 in that model**. This is not a formal-kernel proof and not a complete multiplication theorem. **No new κ.** No supplier, tariff, certificate or selected-frontier value changes.

`research/f7-l22-union-census` (#3818) left five length-22 splits capped: `(10,9)`, `(10,10)`, `(11,9)`, `(11,10)`, `(11,11)`. This PR runs them to completion with the **unchanged** merged engine (SHA256-pinned). It also runs the two 17-point splits `(11,6)` and `(10,7)`, which #3708 had removed only by importing #2773/#2870.

| Split | Cover shards | Nodes | Hits |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `(11,11)` | 251 | 55,385,607,437 | 0 |
| `(11,10)` | 251 | 52,957,641,635 | 0 |
| `(10,10)` | 251 | 44,378,511,529 | 0 |
| `(11,9)` | 251 | 14,058,107,415 | 0 |
| `(10,9)` | 251 | 7,027,617,655 | 0 |
| `(10,7)` | 251 | 700,909 | 0 |
| `(11,6)` | 251 | 2,247 | 0 |

#3708's four necessary conditions leave eleven splits with `s >= t`. #3731 and #3818 excluded `(11,7)`, `(10,8)`, `(11,8)` and `(9,9)`; this PR excludes the other seven. With #2973's `22 <= f(7) <= 24` and even length, f(7) = 24 in the model.

**Cover.** The 203 depth-six restricted-growth prefixes, with `012345` replaced by its 49 depth-eight extensions: 251 shards. The verifier checks that it is a partition: each restricted-growth length-8 word has exactly one prefix in the cover. #3818's depth-four shards were capped. Here the depth-six shard `012345` alone dominated the run time, which is why that shard is expanded.

## Evidence and reproduction

Interpreter: `~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12` (CPython 3.12). From the repository root:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/f7-l22-deep-shard-census          # PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE, 64 s locally
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/f7-l22-deep-shard-census --check-source-history   # PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES
python3.12 -I -B research/f7-l22-deep-shard-census/verify.py --check-receipt --control
python3.12 -I -B research/f7-l22-deep-shard-census/verify.py --replay 11,11 --workers 14     # whole split, opt-in
python3.12 -B research/f7-l22-deep-shard-census/deep_census.py --workers 14 --split 11,11 --split 11,10 --split 11,9 --split 10,10 --split 10,9 --split 10,7 --split 11,6 --work OUT_DIR --output RESULT.json   # regenerate, about 5 CPU-hours
```

- `--check-receipt` checks the engine pin and the cover partition, and rejects two mutated covers: one entry removed, one overlapping entry added. It checks 251 complete zero-hit rows per split, node totals, that the closed splits are exactly #3818's capped splits plus the two 17-point splits, and that all eleven domain rows are closed.
- `--control` compiles the same engine at `(N,L) = (4,8), (4,10), (5,12)`, where universal words exist. On every accepted split (77 splits, 2,452 universal words), a mixed-depth cover's hit set equals the unsharded hit set. A dropped hit-bearing shard is detected.
- `--replay S,T:A:B` recomputes cover slices and requires exact per-shard node equality with `RESULT.json`. Locally I replayed all 251 shards of `(10,9)` in 121 s with 4 workers. All seven splits were run in full locally, and `RESULT.json` was generated by `deep_census.py` from the engine outputs.
- Consistency: #3818's completed `(10,9)` depth-four shards (3.7976e9 nodes) plus the 3,230,011,225 nodes of its capped shard `0123`, run here on depth-six sub-shards, total 7.0276e9. That matches this cover's total up to duplicated prefix nodes.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

- One engine implementation. The seven exclusions rest on `union_census.c` and its written pruning proofs (#2973, #3005/#3818). A second implementation at length 22 has not been run.
- The eleven-row domain is taken from #3708's table, not re-derived in `verify.py`. #3708's rotation symmetry `(s,t) ~ (t,s)` is used as proved there.
- CI replays about 1.2e9 of the 1.74e11 nodes, as registered tail slices of the five large splits plus the two 17-point splits in full. The full replay is opt-in.
- No independent human or formal-kernel review.

## Open next questions

1. Does a separately implemented census (for example #3005's C++ engine, with its `L <= 20` gate lifted) reproduce the seven exclusions on the same cover?
2. Can `verify.py` re-derive #3708's eleven-row domain from the four conditions, so the closure check is self-contained?

## Related open work

- #3899 (1337isnot1337): independent tiny-domain audit of #3818's union prune at `(n,L) = (4,8)`. That is the same engine and prune, on a different domain. Overlapping number: its 22 universal words for split `(4,4)` agree with this engine at `N=4, L=8` (`hits=22`, checked). Its note on the `all_restored_leaves` field does not affect this PR, which uses only `complete`, `hits` and `nodes`.
- No other open PR studies the f(7) word census (checked open PR titles and bodies and #1166).

## CI notes

Green on head `9d21222` (plan pass; replay pass in 2m51s). The CI log shows the receipt check, the control and all five tail slices passing, with exact per-shard node equality: `(10,9)` 247,861,718 nodes, `(11,9)` 218,481,046, `(11,11)` 192,875,091, `(11,10)` 155,724,508 and `(10,10)` 159,403,932, each in 12–22 s. The 17-point splits passed in full.

The first CI run, on `35e1973`, failed because of a timeout in my own registration. A 1.99e9-node `(10,9)` slice exceeded its 150 s budget on the hosted runner. The second commit shrinks every slice to at most 2.5e8 nodes; the claim and receipts are unchanged.
